title: Session 4: T-SQL Language Elements, Data Types, and Operators — SQL Server

questions.questionText: Transact-SQL (T-SQL) is Microsoft's implementation of which standard?
questions.explanation: Transact-SQL (T-SQL) is Microsoft's proprietary extension and implementation of the ANSI standard SQL.

questions.questionText: In the logical order of processing a SELECT statement, which clause is evaluated immediately after WHERE?
questions.explanation: The logical processing order of SELECT is FROM -> WHERE -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> SELECT -> ORDER BY.

questions.questionText: A set, in the context of set theory, is best described as:
options: An ordered list of duplicate values
A collection of distinct objects considered as a whole
A sorted copy of a table
questions.correctAnswer: A collection of distinct objects considered as a whole
questions.explanation: In mathematical set theory, a set is a collection of distinct objects considered as a whole.

questions.questionText: How many types of Transact-SQL statements does SQL Server support, as described in this session?
questions.explanation: T-SQL statements are categorized into three main types: DDL, DML, and DCL.

questions.questionText: Which set operator returns distinct rows produced by both the left and right input queries?
questions.explanation: INTERSECT returns only distinct rows that are output by both the left and right operational queries.

questions.questionText: Which language is used to define and manage all attributes and properties of a database, such as row layouts, column definitions, key columns, file locations, and storage strategy?
questions.explanation: Data Definition Language (DDL) is used to create, modify, and manage database structures and schema definitions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a DDL statement?
questions.explanation: CREATE TABLE is a Data Definition Language (DDL) statement.

questions.questionText: For each database object, DDL usually provides which three statements?
questions.explanation: DDL operations typically provide CREATE (to build), ALTER (to modify), and DROP (to delete) objects.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is used to select, insert, update, or delete data in the objects defined with DDL?
questions.explanation: Data Manipulation Language (DML) statements manage and query data stored within database objects.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a DML statement?
questions.explanation: GRANT is a Data Control Language (DCL) statement used for permissions, not DML.

questions.questionText: Which language is used to control permissions on database objects?
questions.explanation: Data Control Language (DCL) manages authorization, user access, and security permissions.

questions.questionText: Which three statements are the basic DCL statements?
questions.explanation: DCL security control consists of GRANT (give permissions), REVOKE (remove permissions), and DENY (explicitly block).

questions.questionText: Which of the following applications of set theory corresponds to defining unique keys in a table?
options: Acting on the whole set at once
Elements in the set must be unique
questions.correctAnswer: Elements in the set must be unique
questions.explanation: Set theory mandates that elements of a set are distinct, which translates directly to primary/unique keys.

questions.questionText: A data type is best described as:
options: An attribute defining the type of data an object can contain
questions.correctAnswer: An attribute defining the type of data an object can contain
questions.explanation: A data type specifies the classification of data, its storage format, and the allowable values/operations.

questions.questionText: Which of the following objects has a data type?
questions.explanation: In SQL Server, columns, parameters, variables, and expressions all possess an associated data type.

questions.questionText: Which are the two mathematical fundamentals used in SQL Server 2019 for querying data?
questions.explanation: Relational database querying is rooted fundamentally in Set Theory and Predicate Logic.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT one of the three kinds of data types in SQL Server 2019?
questions.explanation: SQL Server 2019 supports system-supplied (system-defined), alias, and CLR user-defined types (UDTs).

questions.questionText: How much memory does a column of type int occupy?
questions.explanation: The standard integer data type (int) in SQL Server requires 4 bytes (32 bits) of storage.

questions.questionText: What is the range of values that the smallint data type can hold?
questions.explanation: smallint occupies 2 bytes (16 bits) and supports values from -32,768 to 32,767.

questions.questionText: Which data type occupies one byte of memory and holds integer values from 0 to 255?
questions.explanation: tinyint occupies 1 byte (8 bits) and stores unsigned integers ranging from 0 to 255.

questions.questionText: Which data type occupies 8 bytes and can hold values from -2^63 to 2^63-1?
questions.explanation: bigint occupies 8 bytes (64 bits) and stores large integers from -9,223,372,036,854,775,808 to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807.

questions.questionText: Which exact numeric data type has a fixed precision and scale?
questions.explanation: numeric (or decimal) is an exact numeric data type with user-defined fixed precision (p) and scale (s).

questions.questionText: In Transact-SQL, WHERE and CASE expressions are based on which mathematical framework?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters and CASE expressions evaluate predicates to TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN based on predicate logic.

questions.questionText: Which approximate numeric data type occupies four bytes of memory?
questions.explanation: real occupies 4 bytes of memory (equivalent to float(24)) as an approximate numeric data type.

questions.questionText: Which data type stores character data that is variable-length and non-Unicode, with a maximum of 8,000 characters?
questions.explanation: varchar stores variable-length, non-Unicode 8-bit characters up to a limit of 8,000 characters (or varchar(max)).

questions.questionText: Which data type stores Unicode character data of fixed length?
questions.explanation: nchar stores fixed-length Unicode characters (2 bytes per character, up to 4,000 characters).

questions.questionText: In the logical order of processing the SELECT statement, which clause is evaluated last?
questions.explanation: ORDER BY is logically evaluated last, ordering the presentation of the materialized result set.

questions.questionText: Which data type stores variable-length binary data with a maximum length of 2^30-1 bytes?
questions.explanation: The legacy image data type stores variable-length binary data up to 2^31-1 (approx. 2 GB) of data.

questions.questionText: Alias data types are:
options: Provided only by SQL Server for internal use
Used only for variables, never columns
questions.explanation: Alias data types allow developers to give custom business names and nullability constraints based on native system data types.

questions.questionText: Which statement is used to create an alias data type?
questions.explanation: The CREATE TYPE statement defines an alias data type or a CLR user-defined type.

questions.questionText: What does the statement CREATE TYPE usertype FROM varchar(20) NOT NULL do?
options: Creates an alias data type named usertype based on varchar(20) that does not allow nulls
Creates a stored procedure named usertype
questions.correctAnswer: Creates an alias data type named usertype based on varchar(20) that does not allow nulls
questions.explanation: CREATE TYPE usertype FROM varchar(20) NOT NULL defines an alias type named usertype based on varchar(20) preventing null values.

questions.questionText: User-defined types in SQL Server are created using:
options: Programming languages supported by the .NET Framework
questions.correctAnswer: Programming languages supported by the .NET Framework
questions.explanation: CLR user-defined types (UDTs) are written in .NET languages (such as C#) and registered into SQL Server assemblies.

questions.questionText: Predicates in Transact-SQL are used to evaluate whether an expression is:
questions.explanation: T-SQL implements three-valued logic (3VL), evaluating conditions to TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN.

questions.questionText: Which predicate specifies a range of values to test?
questions.explanation: BETWEEN tests whether a value falls within an inclusive range: value BETWEEN low AND high.

questions.questionText: Which predicate determines whether a specified value matches any value in a subquery or a list?
questions.explanation: The IN predicate tests if an operand matches any member of a specified explicit list or subquery result.

questions.questionText: Which predicate is used to match characters against a specified pattern?
questions.explanation: LIKE tests character strings against wildcard pattern strings (e.g. %, _, [], [^]).

questions.questionText: The CONTAINS predicate will work only on a table that has:
questions.explanation: CONTAINS is a full-text search predicate and requires full-text indexing on the queried column(s).

questions.questionText:
What is the result of the following code?
DECLARE @Number int;
SET @Number = 2 + 2 * (4 + (5 - 3))
SELECT @Number
questions.explanation: Following operator precedence: (5 - 3) = 2; (4 + 2) = 6; 2 * 6 = 12; 2 + 12 = 14.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT one of the four types of functions in SQL Server 2019 described in this session?
questions.explanation: SQL Server 2019 categorizes built-in functions into Rowset, Aggregate, Ranking, and Scalar functions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an aggregate function?
questions.explanation: SUM is an aggregate function that performs a calculation across a set of values and returns a single value.

questions.questionText: Which of the following are ranking functions?
questions.explanation: The four standard T-SQL ranking functions are RANK(), DENSE_RANK(), NTILE(), and ROW_NUMBER().

questions.questionText: In scalar functions, the input and output are:
options: A single value and a single value
A set of rows and a single value
questions.correctAnswer: A single value and a single value
questions.explanation: Scalar functions operate on a single value and return a single scalar value.

questions.questionText: A local variable name in Transact-SQL must be prefixed with:
questions.explanation: Local user-defined variables in T-SQL always begin with a single at sign (@).

questions.questionText: In SQL Server 2019, what are the in-built system variables prefixed with two '@' signs (such as @@VERSION) categorized as?
questions.explanation: Identifiers starting with @@ are system scalar functions (such as @@VERSION, @@ERROR, @@ROWCOUNT), not global variables.

questions.questionText: Which statement provides branching control based on a logical test in Transact-SQL?
questions.explanation: IF...ELSE provides conditional branching control in T-SQL based on a Boolean condition.

questions.questionText: Which control-of-flow statement defines the structure for exception and error handling?
questions.explanation: BEGIN TRY...END TRY BEGIN CATCH...END CATCH handles errors and exceptions in T-SQL.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct way to write a single-line comment in T-SQL?
questions.explanation: T-SQL single-line comments begin with two hyphens (--).

questions.questionText: Multi-line comments in T-SQL begin with ______ and end with ______.
questions.explanation: Block comments in T-SQL are enclosed within /* and */.

questions.questionText: Which keyword signals the end of a batch in Transact-SQL?
questions.explanation: GO is a batch separator recognized by SQL Server client tools (SSMS, SQLCMD) to submit batches to the server.

questions.questionText: In the logical order of processing a SELECT statement, which clause is evaluated first?
questions.explanation: The FROM clause is the very first clause evaluated in logical query processing, identifying source tables and joins.
